incidents.vector: A CISA contractor accidentally published privileged Amazon AWS GovCloud access keys to a public GitHub repository, discovered by a security researcher in May 2026.
incidents.impact: CISA took the repo offline, revoked access and rotated all secrets; log analysis found none of the leaked credentials were used outside CISA and no customer or mission data was exposed. The agency published a forensic report and new secrets-scanning and GitHub incident playbooks.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a system left unpatched for two years and dwelled in the network for over a week before deploying ransomware.
incidents.impact: Latvia's state forestry firm's mapping, hunting and contractor systems were knocked offline and ~44GB of data (documents, source code, certificates, keys, credentials) was leaked; two-thirds of contract customers still lacked access weeks later. CERT.LV attributed it to a foreign financially-motivated group that also breached pharma firm Olpha.

incidents.vector: The 'Hyadina' ransomware-as-a-service crew deployed a new 'GodDamn' locker, using a Microsoft-signed malicious kernel driver ('PoisonX') in a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver attack to kill security software, alongside AnyDesk RMM, PsExec and 14 open-source credential stealers.
incidents.impact: Symantec observed the group entrench in a victim's environment and deploy ransomware after disabling endpoint protection with the kernel driver, which had been improperly granted a legitimate Microsoft Hardware Compatibility signature.

incidents.victim: Ruckus and ASUS router owners (relay-network infrastructure)
incidents.vector: The China-nexus actor UAT-7810 exploits known (n-day) vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy upgraded 'LONGLEASH' and 'DOGLEASH' backdoors and build Operational Relay Box (ORB) proxy networks.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos reports the group is expanding covert, evasive ORB networks that provide infrastructure for other state-sponsored groups to mask origins and launch attacks against high-value targets.

incidents.victim: Global fraud victims (~142,000 individuals, businesses, governments)
incidents.vector: Coordinated global law-enforcement action (Interpol 'Operation First Light') against social-engineering scam and money-laundering networks — including business email compromise, romance scams, sextortion and investment fraud.
incidents.impact: Authorities arrested more than 5,800 alleged cybercriminals, seized $293 million and blocked over 31,000 bank accounts across 97 countries over three months; investigators uncovered scam centers and a fake police-station replica used to deceive victims.

incidents.victim: Global website owners (many Australian SMBs impacted)
incidents.vector: A large-scale campaign scans for and exploits known vulnerabilities in CMS software and plugins (WordPress, Craft CMS, Joomla JCE and others) enabling unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF or deserialization to deploy webshells.
incidents.impact: Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert warning that compromised web servers are being used for defacement, credential capture, malware hosting and as a pathway to broader network compromise; the agency listed 16+ actively exploited CVEs.

incidents.victim: Five US companies (nonprofit, financial services, hospitality)
incidents.vector: A DigitalMint ransomware negotiator, Angelo Martino, acted as an insider 'double agent' — secretly feeding victims' negotiating positions and insurance limits to Blackcat/AlphV affiliates via backchannels to inflate ransoms, and colluding to deploy the ransomware himself.
incidents.impact: Martino was sentenced to 70 months in prison after helping extort a combined $75.3 million from five US victims (including a $26.8M and a $25.7M payment); authorities seized $10M in assets. Two co-conspirators were previously sentenced to four years each.

incidents.vector: A Go-based backdoor tracked as 'GigaWiper' combines command-and-control with multiple destructive modules — a physical-disk wiper, a fake-ransomware encryptor (derived from Crucio) that discards keys, and a re-implemented FlockWiper — as on-demand commands.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed compromised environments wiped at the physical disk level and rebooted, with irreversible file encryption; the modular design consolidates several standalone destructive tools into a single implant.

incidents.vector: An elevation-of-privilege zero-day in Windows Defender ('RoguePlanet', CVE-2026-50656, CVSS 7.8) was publicly disclosed with a proof-of-concept exploit by a researcher feuding with Microsoft, allowing escalation from standard user to SYSTEM.
incidents.impact: Microsoft issued an out-of-band patch ahead of Patch Tuesday; exploitation status is disputed (Microsoft says not exploited, one vendor claimed in-the-wild use). As a post-compromise tool it could enable security tampering, credential dumping and persistence.

incidents.victim: Taiwanese politicians, academics, journalists and civil society
incidents.vector: Two Taiwanese businessmen were charged with collecting LINE messaging accounts and leasing them (~$162 each) to a Chinese firm linked to China's cyber forces, which impersonated international journalists to build trust and lure targets into installing malware disguised as encrypted communications software.
incidents.impact: Taiwan's Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau tied the scheme to a broad Beijing-linked phishing campaign (documented by ICIJ and Citizen Lab) targeting journalists, activists and Uyghur, Tibetan, Hong Kong and Taiwanese communities via 100+ malicious domains.

incidents.vector: A lone financially-motivated attacker used agentic AI workflows to accelerate reconnaissance, tooling and command structuring, gaining an AWS access key via an internet-facing application weakness and chaining flaws across app services, source repos, CI/CD pipelines and data stores.
incidents.impact: Sygnia reported the attacker compromised a large AWS environment in ~72 hours (work that normally takes weeks), performing secrets theft, backdoor creation and data exfiltration, then staging reversible disruptive actions (blocking S3, zeroing ECS services) to pressure the victim into paying an extortion demand.

incidents.victim: Fortinet/Sophos device owners (incl. UK Foreign Office, embassies, councils)
incidents.vector: The 'FortiBleed' campaign uses internet-wide password spraying against Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL services, then extracts device configuration files (including stored credentials) and cracks them offline to gain persistent administrator access.
incidents.impact: An initial access broker ('SantaAd') on the Exploit[.]in forum claimed credentials from 80,000+ corporate firewalls; credentials for the UK Foreign Office, British embassies and local councils are being sold as a $60,000 archive. FortiBleed actors are reportedly collaborating with Inc and Lynx ransomware gangs.

incidents.vector: Nayax detected unusual activity in one of the company's cloud accounts tied to a subsidiary, which it says was immediately blocked and contained.
incidents.impact: The Israeli payments-technology firm disclosed the incident in an SEC Form 6-K; it is working with experts and US/Israeli law enforcement. Core production systems were reportedly unaffected and the company does not believe material information was exposed, though the investigation is ongoing.

incidents.vector: Attackers executed a malicious governance attack that redirected 4.4 trillion BONK coins to their own wallets.
incidents.impact: Roughly $20 million in crypto-assets were stolen from the BONK meme coin; exchanges Upbit and Kraken paused BONK transactions while the incident is investigated.

incidents.vector: A pro-Kurdish group defaced multiple US Army websites, reportedly via 404-page hijacking.
incidents.impact: The defacements displayed pro-Kurdish messages and insults directed at President Trump and the US Ambassador to Türkiye; the incident was cosmetic with no reported data compromise.

incidents.victim: NetNut / Popa botnet (~2 million consumer devices)
incidents.vector: The FBI, with Google, Lumen and Shadowserver, seized hundreds of domains behind NetNut — a residential proxy service (operated by Israeli firm Alarum Technologies) that turned smart TVs and streaming boxes into always-on proxy nodes via bundled SDKs, largely without owner consent.
incidents.impact: The takedown dismantled infrastructure long synonymous with the Popa botnet; Google's GTIG observed 316 distinct threat-actor clusters using NetNut exit nodes in a single week to mask origins for credential theft, scraping and password-spray attacks.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack on a major Japanese telecom compromised email systems (specific vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: The company said the attack exposed approximately 12 million emails.

incidents.vector: A Vidar-stealer malware-as-a-service affiliate lured victims via malvertising to fake cracked-software downloads; loaders built with the Factory-v3 framework, signed with a fabricated 'JustWatch' certificate and inflated with null bytes to evade sandboxes, dropped Vidar plus the XMRig miner using an AMSI bypass.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 identified 43 loader binaries in the April 2026 spike; Vidar harvests browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets while XMRig mines Monero on victim machines across the US and EU.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, SSM Health, Sutter Health
incidents.vector: Two Scattered Spider members used SIM-swapping and voice/SMS phishing to steal employee credentials and breach corporate networks; the group is tied to 120 intrusions across 47 US entities.
incidents.impact: Thalha Jubair and Owen Flowers pleaded guilty in the UK to the August 2024 Transport for London attack that crippled London's transit systems; Flowers also admitted hacking US healthcare providers SSM Health and Sutter Health. Prosecutors say the group's victims paid at least $115 million in ransoms.

incidents.victim: US/international officials, military, journalists, Ukraine officials
incidents.vector: Russian Intelligence Services actors masquerade as automated support accounts for commercial messaging apps (e.g., Signal), phishing high-value targets for verification codes, account PINs and — in evolved tactics — Backup Recovery Keys to hijack accounts and read historical messages.
incidents.impact: FBI and CISA updated a public advisory on the ongoing campaign (tracked as UNC5792/UNC4221) targeting current and former government officials, military personnel, political figures, journalists and officials in Ukraine; a stolen backup key stays valid even after account re-registration until manually rotated.
